clue.text: Run into nook to find plant

indicators.note: one word goes into another, so the first is placed inside the second

blocks.note: to run, as water does, is to flow
a nook is a corner of a room

explanation.surface: Someone poking into a corner of the garden to discover a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The run goes inside the nook: CORN-FLOW-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornflower is a blue-flowered wild plant of grain fields, so it is one example of the general category.

clue.text: Trespasser in time gets less polite

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time
comparative of rude, impolite

explanation.surface: A trespasser who, given time, becomes more and more rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enters property without permission is an intruder; the words are near synonyms for an unwelcome entrant.

clue.text: No longer healthy to breathe out

blocks.note: an ex is something that no longer holds, as in ex-wife
hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: Someone no longer fit enough to breathe out properly.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhale is the verb for expelling air from the lungs, the opposite of inhaling.

clue.text: Male animal on air is weary

indicators.note: something on air is broadcast, so we hear the word spoken rather than see it spelt

blocks.note: a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A male animal on the radio sounds tired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weary' is a verb here: to bore someone is to weary them.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore someone is to tire them with dullness, which is what wearying a listener means.

clue.text: Idiot to ring spies Edward joined

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
O is ring-shaped
the CIA is the US intelligence agency
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A fool telephones the spies, and someone called Edward joins in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call but is the letter-shaped O.
explanation.definitionFit: Associated means linked or connected with something, so it can stand in for joined as an adjective.

clue.text: Engaged epic duo to dance around clubs

indicators.note: letters set dancing move about and land in a new order
the rearranged letters go around something, enclosing it

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A famous dancing pair, engaged to perform, dance around the nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone line or toilet that is engaged is in use, which is what occupied means.

clue.text: Entrance with a posh pud

blocks.note: a gate is a way in
taken as written
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U speech

explanation.surface: A grand entrance with a posh pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is a crossword staple from the 1950s U and non-U debate. Pud is British slang for pudding, i.e. dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich layered cream cake served as a dessert, so it is one kind of pudding.

clue.text: Overcome echo in club

indicators.note: one item sits in another, inside its letters

blocks.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball
Echo is the NATO alphabet word for E

explanation.surface: Someone overcome by an echo inside a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat an opponent is to defeat or get the better of them, the verb sense of overcome.

clue.text: Old boy with new cow, perhaps, promises to be offensive

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
N is the abbreviation for new
a cow is one example of the bovine animal; 'perhaps' marks it as a loose example
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A former pupil with a new cow and a bundle of promises seems bound to be unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: An old boy is a former pupil of a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: Obnoxious describes someone extremely unpleasant or objectionable, the same idea as offensive in the sense of causing displeasure.

clue.text: Bird dashed into church

indicators.note: one part goes into another, ending up enclosed

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
to dash is to run, past tense ran

explanation.surface: A bird flew hurriedly into a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The crane is a tall long-legged wading bird, one example of the general class.

clue.text: European sailor managed to return report

indicators.note: to return is to come back the way you went, so the string is read from the end

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a tar is an old word for a sailor
to manage a business is to run it, past tense ran

explanation.surface: A European seaman managed to come back and file a report.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell or give an account of events, which is the verb sense of report.

clue.text: Let up on revolting rich

indicators.note: revolting means rising in revolt, so the letters overturn their order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A plea to ease off criticism of the disgusting wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting rich' reads as disgusting plutocrats, but revolting signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means wealthy and luxurious, showing great riches, so it fits rich as an adjective.

clue.text: Avoid removing top after length to gatekeeper's house

indicators.note: taking off the top of a down-style word means losing its opening letter
one piece comes after another, setting their order

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for length
to dodge is to avoid

explanation.surface: Instructions for steering clear of a gatekeeper's house on a long route.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodge is a small house at the gates of a large estate, where the gatekeeper traditionally lived.

clue.text: Southern private investigator has custom that's unworldly

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
PI is the abbreviation for private investigator
a ritual is a customary practice

explanation.surface: A detective from the South follows an otherworldly custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritual concerns the soul rather than material things, so it means not of this world.

clue.text: Something hanging from roof in untidy attic with musty surroundings

indicators.note: an untidy room is in disorder, so these letters are jumbled
surroundings lie all around something, enclosing it

blocks.note: musty air is stale
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something dangling from the rafters in a messy, stale-smelling loft.
explanation.walkthrough: The mnemonic: stalactites hold tight to the ceiling, stalagmites grow up from the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalactite is an icicle-shaped mineral deposit that grows downward from a cave ceiling.

clue.text: The French way to holiday spot is only course available

blocks.note: la is the French feminine article
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a resort is a holiday destination; 'to' joins it to the street

explanation.surface: A French road to a holiday destination is the only route you can take.
explanation.definitionFit: A last resort is the final option left when everything else has failed, so it is the sole remaining choice.

clue.text: Where's tradesman travelling for charity?

indicators.note: things travelling move from where they were, so the letters shift around

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking where a travelling tradesman might be collecting for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity in its older sense is loving kindness towards others, the quality of having a generous, kindly heart.

clue.text: Atmosphere heard to hang over family treasure

indicators.note: what is heard is spoken, so the word is taken for its sound

blocks.note: the air is the atmosphere
to loom is to hang threateningly over something

explanation.surface: A tense mood seems to hang over a precious family possession.
explanation.definitionFit: An heirloom is a valued object handed down through generations, hence a treasure of the family.

clue.text: Put bird products on inferno to produce fine porcelain

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece put on another sits above it

blocks.note: birds lay eggs
the Inferno is hell, as in Dante

explanation.surface: A recipe of eggs over a blazing fire that yields delicate china.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell porcelain is an extremely thin, translucent china named for its likeness to the shell of an egg.

clue.text: Left holding stiffly formal article, getting severe reproof

indicators.note: something holding other things keeps them inside it

blocks.note: red is the colour of the political left
prim means stiffly proper
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A left-winger clutching a stuffy item earns a harsh telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprimand is a formal rebuke given by someone in authority, which is a stern reproof.

clue.text: Sharp petty officer popular outside of Torquay

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its two ends, the letters around the edge

blocks.note: PO is the abbreviation for petty officer
in means fashionable or popular
the first and last letters of the town's name

explanation.surface: A smart naval officer, well liked, out on the edge of Torquay.
explanation.walkthrough: Torquay is a seaside resort in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointy means having a sharp tip, so it can replace sharp as an adjective.

clue.text: Row about German feline

indicators.note: about means around, so one part wraps round the other

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: An argument about a German cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but means a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger is the largest member of the cat family, so it is a feline by classification.

clue.text: Tool runs into dryer

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other and ends up enclosed

blocks.note: a towel is something you dry yourself with
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A tool that has got tangled inside a tumble dryer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand implement for gardening or plastering, an example of a tool.

clue.text: One of three allowed to follow tour

indicators.note: one piece follows another, so it comes second

blocks.note: a tour is a trip
let means allowed

explanation.surface: One member of a group of three is permitted to come on a tour.
explanation.definitionFit: A triplet is one of three children born at the same birth, so it is one of a trio.

clue.text: Dull carpeting returned by European

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word runs the other way

blocks.note: a mat is a piece of floor covering
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Boring floor covering sent back by a European customer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tame can mean unexciting or insipid, as in a tame ending, the same sense as dull.

clue.text: He wears fool's garments

indicators.note: whatever is worn is on the outside, so one part wraps around the other

blocks.note: a clot is a fool, and the 's adds its S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man dresses in a jester's costume.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'fool's' is used as a plain S tacked onto the fool, and that whole word wraps around HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes are the items worn on the body, the everyday word for garments.

clue.text: Stretch a point to include male

indicators.note: the phrase is said to include something, so the letters sit inside its words

blocks.note: running across the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Bending the truth slightly so as to let a man in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretch a point' reads as an idiom for exaggerating, but it is just the string of letters holding the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is informal British for a man or fellow, so it names an adult male person.

clue.text: Oddly deficient importation logo

indicators.note: lacking the odd ones means only the even-placed characters survive

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: An imported company emblem that is strangely lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the odd letters of 'importation' and the even ones remain.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto is a short phrase representing an organisation, close to a logo as a slogan or emblem of identity.

clue.text: Bank clerk accepting rupees and vatu, initially for tourist

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so it goes inside
initially points to the opening letter of each word

blocks.note: a teller is a cashier in a bank
the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A bank cashier handles rupees and vatu, foreign currency for a tourist.
explanation.walkthrough: The vatu is the currency of Vanuatu; only its first letter matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller is someone on a journey, and a tourist is a traveller visiting places for pleasure.
